resources.string: Audio and GPS checks
Start each check yourself. Checks stop when you leave this screen. No audio or location is saved.
Confirm you are parked and stop the projection connection to enable checks.

Microphone: a 5-second live level meter. Speakers: quiet left, then right tones at your current media volume. Other media may pause during audio checks. These check Android audio, not the phone or adapter microphone.
Test microphone
Test speakers
Check GPS fix
Stop check
Open check permissions
Microphone and precise location permissions are needed for their respective checks. Speaker testing needs neither.
Input level: %1$d%%
Highest input level: %1$d%%
The input reached clipping level. Try speaking more softly or moving away from the microphone.
Listening for 5 seconds. Speak normally.
Playing left, then right. Tap Stop check to end early.
Waiting up to 22 seconds for a fresh GPS fix. A clear view of the sky helps.
Check finished. A changing level confirms audio samples; a flat meter can mean silence, the wrong input, or a system restriction.
Tones sent. Confirm that you heard both sides. If you heard nothing, check media volume and the head-unit audio route.
Fresh GPS fix received. Reported accuracy: ±%1$d m. This checks the head unit, not GPS delivery to the phone.
Check stopped.
Permission is missing or was revoked. Open permissions, then try again.
Check unavailable. For audio, finish any call and check the audio route. For GPS, enable Android location and check that the head unit has a GPS receiver.
No result before the time limit. For GPS, move to a clear view of the sky and try again. This does not prove a hardware fault.
The microphone stream stopped delivering samples. Check microphone permission and the input route, then try again. This differs from receiving silent audio.
Android audio playback stopped making progress. Check the media output route and try again; the test could not confirm that both tones played.
